A miniature sculptural landscape made entirely from carefully folded and torn fine-art papers sits on a single low, broad, warm ivory stone plinth. Three asymmetrical paper ridgelines in burnt sienna, soft terracotta, and pale apricot rise gracefully from left to middle; visibly thin folded edges, delicate paper fibers, tactile matte surfaces, sophisticated handcrafted construction. A narrow winding river cut from glossy translucent deep teal glass travels through the folds and flows into one perfectly calm shallow pool at the front right of the plinth. One very small ivory paper arch spans the river near the center. A single translucent amber disc floats low behind the tallest ridge like an abstract setting sun. These are original imaginary forms, not an existing artwork or landmark.

Composition: a horizontal 3:2 image, elegant off-center sculptural arrangement, complete plinth visible, camera at a low three-quarter angle, generous quiet negative space in the upper third and along the right side. No people, no animals, no plants, no text, no logos, no watermark, no additional objects. This is a physical fine-art still-life photograph, not flat illustration, not a poster mockup, not CGI-looking plastic.

Lighting: a large warm golden-hour beam from upper left gives long soft-edged shadows; gentle cool ambient fill preserves shadow detail; the teal glass catches small realistic highlights and subtle caustics on the cream stone.
